column2: David's rising and departure and Jonathan's entry into the city remain at this chapter's selected opening, not reassigned to chapter 20.
David reaches Nomba and Abimelech, whose astonishment prompts the question about being alone. Both selected names remain rather than Nob and Ahimelech substitutions.
David reports a confidential royal commission today and his solemn instruction of the young men at God's Faithfulness, Phellani Allemoni. The names and command details remain as David's claim.
column3: The relation of the gloss God's Faithfulness to Phellani Allemoni remains uncertain; it is not silently reduced to an anonymous such-and-such place.

column2: The request names five loaves conditionally and asks for what is available; at hand and give me express the hand-based availability and transfer without introducing more bread.
Common and holy loaves contrast, with only supported by the exceptive construction; the young men's abstention from a woman is followed by singular he may eat.
column3: The singular eating subject is not silently pluralized; its connection to David or a representative person remains unresolved.

column2: Propose because of my equipment rather than through my equipment: dia takes the accusative and is naturally causal here. Abstention, yesterday-and-third-day wording, all young men purified, the common road and its future sanctification remain.
column3: The equipment and road relation is still obscure; correcting the causal preposition does not establish a ritual mechanism or license a reconstructed different source reading.

column2: Abimelech gives the loaves of presentation because only Presence loaves were available, removed before the Lord to replace with hot bread that day; both bread designations remain.
column3: The subject of took them is implicit; the inherited he preserves the unresolved reference rather than naming a priestly routine not explicitly stated.

column2: Doeg is a Syrian tending Saul's mules, detained neessaran before the Lord on that day; none of these distinctive details is harmonized to Edomite and chief shepherd.
column3: The opaque neessaran and its relation to detained remain unresolved.

column2: David asks about an available spear or sword and explains missing sword and equipment by the king's urgent matter. This remains his explanation, not independent narrative confirmation.
Both Behold markers, Goliath's sword, Valley of Elah, garment wrapping, conditional taking, absence of another sword and David's none-like-it reply remain.
The sword is given, David flees that day from Saul and comes to Achish king of Gath; the selected giving sentence remains at this unit's start.
Achish's servants call David king of the land and quote the women's numerical song. Authored line breaks preserve the two song lines inside the nested question without changing words.
David puts the words in his heart and greatly fears Achish king of Gath; the bodily reception image and named object of fear remain.
Altered face, feigning that day, drumming on city doors, being carried about in his hands, falling against gate doors and running saliva all remain.
column3: The passive/middle carried-about phrase and its hand reference remain difficult; no modern diagnosis or extra graphic behavior is supplied.

column2: Achish points with Behold and see to a man subject to fits and asks why he was brought; this remains the character's description, not a narrator's medical finding.
Achish asks whether he lacks such people, describes the proposed behavior before him and denies entry into a house. The selected a house is not changed to my house.
David leaves, escapes and comes to Adullam's cave; his brothers and paternal house hear and descend to him. The whole family group remains.
Three repeated everyone groups name need, debt and pain of soul, followed by David's leadership and about four hundred men.
At Mizpeh of Moab David asks the king to host both parents until he knows what God will do for him; both family members and temporal condition remain.
David entreats the Moabite king, and his parents remain through David's whole stronghold period.
column3: Entreated renders the face-of-the-king idiom without a literal face noun; stronghold for perioche is provisional in this geographic context.

column2: Gad commands departure from the stronghold to Judah; David goes, comes and stays in the city of Sarich. City is not silently changed to forest.
Saul hears David and his men are discovered; his setting is a hill below cultivated ground in Ramah, with spear and attendants. Cultivated ground is not changed to a tree.
The repeated speech introduction addresses Benjamin's sons and asks whether Jesse's son will give all of them fields, vineyards and commands of hundreds and thousands. Both all expressions remain.
Saul accuses all of conspiracy and repeats uncovering his ear about the covenant and his son's raising a servant as enemy; lack of suffering for him is retained as a separate accusation.
Doeg the Syrian, appointed over the mules, reports seeing Jesse's son at Nomba with Abimelech son of Ahitub. The repeated identities align with chapter 21 without harmonizing other witnesses.
Doeg reports divine inquiry, provisions and Goliath's sword; the implied priestly agent remains he in the continuity of the prior unit.
column3: The inquiry is recorded as Doeg's report even though chapter 21's narrated encounter does not explicitly state it; no retroactive addition is made there.

column2: The king summons Abimelech and all his father's priestly sons at Nomba, and all come. The family scope and universal arrival remain.
Saul addresses the son of Ahitub; Here I am and Speak, lord answer with ordinary human honorific usage.
Saul treats bread, sword and divine inquiry as a conspiracy to make David his enemy today. The charge remains Saul's interpretation rather than a narrator verdict.
The priest asks who matches David's faithfulness, royal marriage, command of all orders and renown in the household. No alternate bodyguard title is inserted.
The rhetorical question about beginning inquiry today precedes emphatic denial, a plea against charging servant and paternal house, and professed ignorance of small or great matters.
column3: The precise scope of By no means is interpretive within the defense; it does not automatically deny every prior divine inquiry.

column2: Saul announces certain death for Abimelech and his whole paternal house. The emphatic death construction and collective sentence remain.
Saul orders the runners to bring forward and kill the Lord's priests, citing their hand with David and failure to uncover his ear; the servants refuse to put their own hands against those priests.
The command singles out Doeg, who turns and kills three hundred and five ephoud-bearing priests that day. The selected number, Syrian identity and divine priestly designation remain.
The slaughter extends to priestly Nomba, men and women, infants and nursing children, calves, donkeys and sheep; the complete categories remain without embellishment.
One son, Abiathar, survives Abimelech son of Ahitub and flees after David. One is explicit, not an inferred count of all possible survivors elsewhere.
Abiathar attributes all the priests' deaths to Saul; this does not remove Doeg's executing role in verse 18, since command and execution are distinct agency descriptions.
David recalls knowing Doeg would certainly report to Saul and accepts responsibility for the souls of Abiathar's paternal house; the emphatic report and soul language remain.
Propose For before the explanation of why Abiathar need not fear. David promises to seek a place for Abiathar's soul wherever he seeks for his own, and declares protection with him.
column3: The selected seeking-a-place construction is not replaced by an enemy seeking both lives; the promise's agency stays with David.
